functionalObligations.text: only counterparties on a whitelist may create or destroy the unit; everyone else may only buy and sell it on a secondary market
functionalObligations.note: PARTIAL FIT, and the corpus files this as residue while also carrying Aw. Both are right about different halves. Aw names the gate; it does not name that the gated action is ISSUANCE ITSELF, so that the peg is a right for a named few and an arbitrage outcome for everyone else. In V2 the whitelist moved on-chain and benefactors whitelist their own beneficiaries by contract call (https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/minting-usde/mint-and-redeem-contract-v2.md, accessed 2026-08-04), which makes the gate a delegable authority as well as a list — a second thing Aw does not say.

functionalObligations.text: creation is an atomic exchange against a signed order quoting a price the protocol computed, carrying its own request identifier, executable by contract wallets as well as keys, and priced so that the issuer earns no spread on it
functionalObligations.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus carries no execution element for Ethena. The mint is a request-for-quote in the precise sense of the symbol — a signed maker quote settled atomically — with the RFQ id moved on-chain as order_id inside the signature and signature_type defaulting to EIP712 with EIP-1271 support (https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/minting-usde/mint-and-redeem-contract-v2.md, accessed 2026-08-04). What Rf does not carry is that the quote is the ISSUANCE PRICE OF A LIABILITY rather than a trade in an existing asset, and that slippage and execution cost are priced into it so 'Ethena earns no profit from the minting or redeeming of USDe'.

functionalObligations.text: a whitelisted holder may redeem the unit for backing assets at one dollar at any time, served from about half a percent of backing held as stablecoins inside the minting contract and replenished from about four percent held across custodians
functionalObligations.note: FORCED: Rd as written implies a general right. Law L7's discharge for this application is a redemption right restricted to a whitelist plus a 0.5% on-demand reserve — a par exit for named parties over a fractional buffer, which is a materially weaker guarantee than Rd asserts.

functionalObligations.text: the right to create or destroy the unit is suspended automatically whenever the unit's price diverges unfavourably from its stablecoin reference beyond a configured threshold
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and one of the sharpest in the lane. The V2 mandate delta limit is aimed explicitly at 'blackswan events like stablecoin collateral de-pegging'. Gp names a pause held by an authority; Rd names a right. Neither names a right that voids ITSELF, by rule and with no actor, precisely in the price region where it would be exercised — which is the entire content of this control and inverts the guarantee in F3 exactly when it matters.

functionalObligations.text: creation and destruction are capped per block, separately for stablecoin and non-stablecoin assets, under a global cap adjustable by a development multisig
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. A quantitative speed limit on creating the unit, differentiated by asset class, and the main defence against a compromised minter key. As is quantity adjustment TOWARD A PEG; this is a quantity ceiling per unit time FOR SAFETY, which is a different instrument with a different objective. CROSS-PROTOCOL: the same object is Sky's Hole/hole liquidation throughput cap (sky.json F11), Lista's 500,000/day redemption quota (lista-cdp.json F10) and Spark's regenerating allowance (spark-savings.json F19). Four independent instances of a magnitude-per-time envelope on a permitted action, and no symbol.

functionalObligations.text: the backing is a book of six strategy families — crypto basis, non-crypto basis, DeFi lending, institutional lending, tokenised real-world assets and liquid stablecoins — whose allocation across categories is changed continuously at the operator's discretion
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. At attests to a reserve's existence and value; nothing names 'the reserve's composition is a discretionary investment decision taken continuously'. Sv (servicing & determination discretion) is REJECTED after consideration: Sv names discretion in determining and servicing a CLAIM — calling a default, applying a waterfall — not discretion in choosing what the reserve owns. CORRECTION TO THE CORPUS: the corpus record describes the 2024 design ('long staked ETH and liquid restaking collateral, short an equivalent notional of ETH perpetual futures'). Against the current documentation the crypto basis trade is one family of six, so the corpus's ~20% coverage score for Dp is an overstatement measured against the 2026 mechanism.

functionalObligations.text: the composition and value of the backing, and the balance of the reserve fund, are published on a dashboard and supported by custodian attestations rather than by an on-chain object
functionalObligations.note: FORCED, the same way At is forced for Sky's RWA vaults: At implies an on-chain attestation object and this is a web page plus a custodian's letter. L27 requires named attester, independence, stated assurance, staleness bound and recourse; the custodians are named (Copper, Ceffu, Fireblocks) and the staleness bound and recourse are not stated anywhere I can cite. UNKNOWN on three of five limbs.

functionalObligations.text: volatile holdings are paired with a short futures position of approximately the same notional so that a move in the spot leg is offset by the hedge, and that pairing is re-established continuously as prices move, margin is rebalanced and positions are rolled
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE and FORCED. Dp reads 'directional position & hedge maintenance'; the defining property here is that the book is deliberately NON-directional, and the hedge is not an overlay protecting some other exposure — the hedge IS the reserve asset. Dp is silent on where the position lives (a centralised venue), who maintains it (an off-chain operator), why it exists (to make the backing price-invariant), what it earns (funding), and what happens when the venue fails. The maintained-neutrality invariant is an operational obligation on an off-chain program, checked by no contract, and it is the single largest unnamed object in a $3.9bn protocol.

functionalObligations.text: the protocol's revenue is the funding payment of perpetual markets it does not operate and does not govern, received as an ordinary external participant
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Pf is NOT USED, deliberately: Pf is the transfer a perp exchange implements between its own longs and shorts. Ethena implements no such transfer; it takes one from Binance (50%), Bybit (25%), OKX (15%), Deribit (5%) and Bitget (5%). Using Pf here would assert that Ethena runs a perpetual market, which is false. This is a clean DIRECTIONAL gap: every risk-transfer symbol in the vocabulary is written from the issuer's side and there is no way to name being the counterparty to someone else's mechanism.

functionalObligations.text: the backing never sits on the venue that holds the hedge: it is held by named third-party settlement providers in bankruptcy-remote structures and only delegated to derivatives venues as margin on a rolling four-hour cycle, so that on a venue's failure positions are treated as closed and exposure is limited to unsettled profit and loss between cycles
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, confirmed verbatim against the current docs. Copper (Clearloop), Ceffu and Fireblocks; 'in the event of Copper's failure, users' funds are not a part of the Copper estate'; Copper settles PnL daily; the protocol 'is reliant upon the cooperation and legal behavior of our Off-Exchange Settlement provider partners'. Two unnamed objects in one obligation: off-exchange settlement and custody mirroring, and venue/counterparty concentration as a risk the design deliberately trades against custodial risk. The vocabulary has no custody sort at all — Xf moves an asset between domains, and there is nothing for an asset that stays put while its economic effect is mirrored somewhere else.

functionalObligations.text: the prices used to quote creation and redemption are computed by an off-chain service that ingests six centralised venues plus two oracle networks, normalises and validates them, and publishes the result; no contract reads a price feed to test solvency
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE: the corpus carries Ex for Ethena and this construction drops it. Ex names an on-chain oracle with an on-chain consumer. Here the price service, the order router, the position reconciliation service and the monitoring systems are a private program run by a company (https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/hedging-system.md, accessed 2026-08-04), and the on-chain mandate delta limit of F4 compares the order's own implied price against its reference rather than reading a feed. The largest synthetic dollar in the category has no on-chain price oracle, which is a stronger statement than the corpus's Ex records and changes which laws even apply.

functionalObligations.text: holding the unit pays nothing; staking it mints a share whose price rises as an off-chain distributor transfers realised revenue into the vault
functionalObligations.note: StakedUSDeV2 (0x9d39a5de30e57443bff2a8307a4256c8797a3497) is ERC-4626 and the staking contract IS the share token. Ix is FORCED in the way the corpus records: the index moves because an operator transferred realised profit in, not because an on-chain accrual computed it. 'Two instruments the vocabulary treats as one' — the unstaked unit and the staked share have different economics and Sh + Ix cannot say that one of them pays nothing by design.

functionalObligations.text: revenue is transferred in periodically and vests linearly across the interval rather than landing at once, so that a deposit made just before a transfer cannot capture it
functionalObligations.note: FLAGGED rather than claimed, following stage 1. Transfers every 8 hours vesting linearly over 8 hours, and the Foundation deliberately pays in several smaller instalments through the week to deny arbitrage (https://docs.ethena.fi/protocol-overview/rewards-mechanism.md, accessed 2026-08-04). Sr names the shape exactly and gets the reason wrong: here streaming is an MEV defence, not a product feature. Same shape, different justification, and the vocabulary cannot record the difference — which matters because removing the stream would not remove a feature, it would open an attack.

functionalObligations.text: the share price can only rise or stay flat: periods in which the cost of maintaining positions exceeds revenue are absorbed by a reserve fund, and the share of ongoing revenue directed to that fund is a governance parameter currently set to zero, with all revenue going to incentive rewards and promotional distributions instead
functionalObligations.note: Bs is FORCED: the reserve absorbs the loss first, so it is first-loss, but it is protocol-owned treasury rather than staked third-party capital exposed to slashing, and 'slashable' is the operative word in Bs. SHARPENING THE CORPUS: a first-loss buffer with a zero accrual rate is a different object from a first-loss buffer, and the vocabulary cannot say that a backstop is not being funded. Em covers the destination of the revenue.

functionalObligations.text: the staked class stands ahead of the unstaked class in the declared loss order, so that the unit's holders bear a shortfall the share's holders do not
functionalObligations.note: FORCED: a two-class waterfall in substance, with no attachment points, no separately priced tranche instruments, and a seniority asserted in documentation rather than enforced by a settlement contract. L6 requires (Sv | mechanical trigger) + declared seniority + dispute forum + recovery-timing assumption; only declared seniority is present, and the dispute forum is a company.

functionalObligations.text: the level of the payout is decided off-chain: a foundation subsidiary calculates an annual percentage yield weekly as part of internal accounting and executes it as a transfer, and no rate anywhere in the system is set to defend the peg
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the finding this obligation exists to record. Ethena is the one protocol of the five with NO price-of-credit instrument at all: the peg is defended purely by primary-market arbitrage between whitelisted parties (F1, F3), and the payout is a distribution of realised profit rather than a price set to move supply or demand. Written beside the other four — Sky's bounded delegate (sky.json F5-F10), USDD's external-benchmark reaction function (usdd.json F6), Lista's closed-loop controller (lista-cdp.json F6) and Liquity's borrower-chosen rate (liquity.json F5) — this makes five species, not one gap. It also refines the corpus's category residue, which asserts that the price of credit is 'the instrument all five actually use': four of five use it, and the largest by TVL does not.

functionalObligations.text: an unwhitelisted holder exits by unstaking through a cooldown that parks the unit in a separate contract for a period the administrator may set to anything up to ninety days
functionalObligations.note: USDeSilo holds the parked balance; setCooldownDuration admits values up to 90 days at admin discretion. Wq names the queue and not that ITS LENGTH IS A LEVER THE OPERATOR MAY PULL — the difference between a queue that reflects backing illiquidity and a queue that can be extended to ninety days by a transaction is the whole of L14's content, and the symbol carries neither.

functionalObligations.text: two multisigs hold the constructive authority — one may change the supported collateral set and the custodian set, the other may grant and revoke every operational role — and no delay applies to either
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a DEPARTURE twice over. (a) The corpus carries Tg for Ethena; the multisig/timelock matrix specifies NO TIMELOCK DELAY FOR ANY ROLE, so Tg is dropped. (b) The corpus carries Up; the V1-to-V2 transition was a redeployment to a new address (V1 0x2cc440b721d2cafd6d64908d6d8c4acc57f8afc3, V2 0xe3490297a08d6fC8Da46Edb7B6142E4F461b62D3, https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/key-addresses.md, accessed 2026-08-04), i.e. migration by moving the whitelist and the roles, not upgrade in place, so Up is dropped. What remains has no symbol: an authority whose risk is entirely a property of its holder — two multisigs of undisclosed threshold, immediately. The vocabulary names facilities and not holders, which is exactly the gap lane 07 exhibited on the three largest bridges.

functionalObligations.text: twenty minter keys and twenty redeemer keys exist because concurrent throughput demands them, and at least three further keys, held partly by external organisations that are not governors, can disable creation and destruction and strip the operational roles without being able to use them
functionalObligations.note: FORCED, and two unnamed objects. (a) The NUMBER of keys is a capacity parameter — the Redeemer set is deliberately the same twenty addresses as the Minter set 'for handling concurrent load' — so key count is an operational-throughput decision with a security cost, and no symbol carries it. (b) An outsider holds a purely destructive power: Gatekeepers can kill but never mint. Gp names a pause and cannot express that the right to halt is deliberately held by parties who hold no right to act, which is the same accountability split the yield lane found at Spark (spark-savings.json F20). Gatekeeper monitoring runs 'in separate AWS accounts' (https://docs.ethena.fi/technical-design/overview/github-overview.md, accessed 2026-08-04). Governance itself is a rotating committee structure whose docs state that 'fully on-chain governance is not a practical or viable option at present' (https://docs.ethena.fi/protocol-overview/governance.md, accessed 2026-08-04) — so there is no on-chain franchise, no quorum and no delay to decompose.

functionalObligations.text: a named role may mark a holder fully restricted, after which they cannot receive the share, and may move the locked balance of a restricted address to a segregated protocol wallet
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE, and an unusually exact fit — one of the few candidate symbols in this lane that needed no stretching. CORRECTION: the corpus names the role FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKER_ROLE; the docs name it FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKING_ROLE, and record that SOFT_RESTRICTED_STAKING_ROLE exists and has never been used. redistributeLockedAmounts is a documented function rather than an inferred capability, so the fit is tighter than the corpus records. L28 wants named authority + enumerated triggers + appeal path + holder disclosure; only the named authority is present.

functionalObligations.text: the administrator may remove any token except the protocol's own unit from the contract to an address the protocol controls
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. rescueTokens is a standing administrative sweep: a permanent claim on everything that lands in the contract other than the unit itself. Fz covers freeze and forced transfer of the protocol's OWN unit; this is the complement and has no symbol.

functionalObligations.text: the unit, the share and the governance token are issued on many domains, sharing one address triple across most rollups and carrying distinct deployments on non-EVM chains
functionalObligations.note: ENA 0x58538e6A, USDe 0x5d3a1Ff2, sUSDe 0x211Cc4DD on most L2s, with separate deployments on Solana, ZKSync, Zircuit, Aptos and TON. As at USDD (usdd.json F15), Xf asserts a transfer with L9's debit-equals-credit; a shared vanity address across domains is not evidence of a transfer relation, and stage 1 did not establish the bridging path. Carried because multi-domain issuance is real; flagged because the symbol asserts more than the evidence.
